**International Copper Study Group Industry Advisory Panel 28**<sup>**th**</sup> **September 2010, 2.00pm – 4.00pm Antofagasta, Chile** 

**ICSG/IAP10/5** 

# **Industry Advisory Panel Draft Minutes** 

# **1. Opening of the Meeting by the Chairman** 

The Industry Advisory Panel met on 28 September in Antofagasta Chile with the objective of encouraging further industry participation and informing a wider range of copper industry representatives of the work and benefits of the Study Group. Industry advisers were present from Australia, Brazil, Chile, India, Japan, Poland and the United Kingdom along with industry association, government and Study Group representatives. The Chairman opened the proceedings by informing the participants that the Industry Advisory Panel provides an opportunity for industry advisers to meet as a group, raise issues to the attention of government members and provide feedback, guidance and advice to the Group on its priorities, programs and activities. 

# **2. Adoption of the Agenda** 

(Document ICSG/IAP10/3) 

The agenda was adopted as tabled. 

# **3. What the International Copper Study Group is Doing of Relevance to Industry** 

ICSG Chief Statistician Ms Ana Rebelo provided the panel with information about ICSG regular publications including the ICSG Copper Bulletin, Statistical Yearbook and Directories, in addition to providing industry advisors with an update on the establishment of the on-line statistical database scheduled for completion in the first quarter of 2011. 

ICSG Head of Economics and Environment Mr Carlos Risopatron presented a summary of the 2010 Report on Regulatory Developments Affecting Copper, including: multilateral regulatory developments within the UN, OECD and elsewhere; regulations affecting copper in the European Union; Chinese regulations affecting copper; selected regulatory developments in other ICSG member countries; and regulatory developments in non-member countries. 

ICSG Economist Mr Joseph Pickard provided participants with an overview of the 2010 World Copper Factbook and updates on secretariat research on leading indicators of refined copper usage and on exploration and development, including recent trends in copper exploration spending, sources of exploration investment and areas for further Study Group investigation. 

Regarding leading economic indicators, the industry advisor from BHP Billiton suggested looking at other indicators such as Purchasing Managers Indexes and, on the subject of regulations, looking more closely at regulations related to energy efficiency. 

# **4. Presentation on Longer Term Supply and Demand Issues and Factors Affecting Global Copper Markets and Panel Discussion** 

Mr Jon Barnes, Managing Consultant, CRU Analysis, delivered his presentation on longer term supply and demand issues and factors affecting global copper markets over the next 5-plus years. Topics covered included recent trends in per capita copper usage, the impact of high prices i

n the short and long term, the outlook for copper demand in the future including the role of China and developing countries, a breakdown of copper demand by usage category and by function, the potential for substitution, challenges for long term supply, the increasingly important role of copper scrap, an assessment of the value of copper, and the CRU copper price forecast for the next several years. Mr Barnes was then joined by Mr Jurgen Leibbrandt (Codelco), Mr Paul Missen (Anglo American), Mr Tariq Salaria (BHP Billiton) and Mr Radoslaw Zalozinski (KGHM) for a panel discussion. Panellists indicated that some of the key topics affecting copper supply and demand included the geo-political risks associated with bringing supply on-stream, the rising costs of producing copper, problems associated with estimating disruption allowances and the impacts on demand from increasing urbanization and rising per capita consumption of copper. Other subjects addressed included the delays in supply caused by changes in regulatory and tax schemes and the issue of substitution. Specifically, the question was raised as to whether industry associations should spend more resources defending current uses of copper rather than developing new products. While it was generally agreed that relatively high prices and price volatility play a large role in driving substitution, the difficulty in defending all applications from substitution and the need to develop new markets and products were also stressed. The panel also discussed copper’s role as a store of value, including in China, and it was noted that Exchange Traded Funds were an increasing source of investment in copper. # **5. Issues for Possible Future Study Group Attention** (Background Document ICSG/IAP10/4) The secretariat presented industry advisors with a list of key current issues and asked participants to rank the issues in terms of how important it would be to have further information generated by ICSG. The results are presented below; the importance of the Study Group avoiding duplication of the work of other organisations and needing to add value in selecting its activities was emphasised.
